title: 1 Chronicles 23
paragraphs: ¹ When David was old and had lived a full life, he made his son Solomon king over Israel. ² He gathered together all the leaders of Israel, along with the priests and the Levites. ³ The Levites were counted from the age of thirty and upward; the total number, counted man by man, came to thirty-eight thousand. ⁴ Of these, twenty-four thousand were to oversee the work of the house of the LORD; six thousand were officers and judges; ⁵ four thousand were gatekeepers; and four thousand were to praise the LORD with the instruments David had made for that purpose.

⁶ David divided them into groups according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. ⁷ The sons of Gershon were Laadan and Shimei. ⁸ The sons of Laadan: Jehiel the chief, then Zetham and Joel — three in all. ⁹ The sons of Shimei: Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran — three. These were the heads of the families of Laadan. ¹⁰ The sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah — these four were the sons of Shimei.

¹¹ Jahath was the chief and Zizah was second. Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they were counted as a single family. ¹² The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel — four in all. ¹³ The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart to consecrate the most holy things — he and his descendants forever — to burn incense before the LORD, to minister to him, and to pronounce blessings in his name forever. ¹⁴ As for Moses, the man of God, his sons were reckoned as part of the tribe of Levi. ¹⁵ The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.

¹⁶ Of the descendants of Gershom, Shebuel was the chief. ¹⁷ Of the descendants of Eliezer, Rehabiah was the chief. Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah's descendants were very numerous. ¹⁸ Of the sons of Izhar, Shelomith was the chief. ¹⁹ Of the sons of Hebron: Jeriah was the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth. ²⁰ Of the sons of Uzziel: Micah was the first and Isshiah the second.

²¹ The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish. ²² Eleazar died leaving no sons, only daughters. Their kinsmen, the sons of Kish, married them. ²³ The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth — three in all. ²⁴ These were the descendants of Levi, listed by family — the heads of families as registered by name, counted individually. They performed the work of the service in the house of the LORD from the age of twenty years and upward. ²⁵ For David said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, has given rest to his people, and he has come to dwell in Jerusalem forever.

²⁶ And since the Levites will no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of its equipment for its service — ²⁷ for by David's final instructions the Levites were counted from twenty years old and upward — ²⁸ their duty is to assist the sons of Aaron in the service of the house of the LORD, caring for the courts and chambers, purifying all the holy things, and performing every task involved in the service of God's house; ²⁹ also to handle the rows of bread, the fine flour for grain offerings, the wafers of unleavened bread, the baked goods, and the fried offerings, as well as all the measures of quantity and size; ³⁰ and to stand every morning to give thanks and praise to the LORD, and likewise in the evening;

³¹ and to offer all the burnt sacrifices to the LORD on the Sabbaths, the new moon festivals, and the appointed feasts, in the proper number and prescribed manner, continually before the LORD. ³² They were also to be in charge of the tent of meeting and the holy place, and to assist their kinsmen the sons of Aaron in the service of the house of the LORD."
